newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-No hint in Fairfax comments-Alston.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-No hint in Fairfax comments-Alston.

text.p: Australian telecommunications minister Richard Alston said on Wednesday his recent comments about a sale of John Fairfax Group Ltd newspapers gave no hint of government media ownership policy.
Alston said on Sunday that he could "envisage the scenario" where Fairfax paper's The Sydney Morning Herald, The Age and The Australian Financial Review, could be sold to separately.

"I was not in any way talking about any matters directly affecting Fairfax, of course of which I have no knowledge, and I certainly wasn't intending to give any indication of preference on my behalf or the government," Alston told reporters.
He was speaking after giving an address to a meeting of APEC ministers for the telecommunications industry.
"I was simply talking in a context of changes which might be possible, irrespective of the cross-media rules in this country," Alston said.
Alston said commericial considerations would continue to drive the behaviour of media proprietors.
John Fairfax is 25 percent owned by Canadian media baron Conrad Black's The Telegraph Plc.

Black said on Tuesday that Alston's remarks were "wildly inaccurate public musing by the minister for communications regarding the sale of our shareholding or the break-up of the Fairfax Group is no more helpful to any legitimate interest than was the erratic conduct of some of his predecessors."

Black has stated previously that he was interested in raising his Fairfax stake in order to ward off potential predators, such as Australian media barons Rupert Murdoch and Kerry Packer, who between them own over 20 percent of Fairfax.
"Mr black has stated several times that he would like an increase in the level of his holding in the Fairfax group," Alston said.
"That is a decision for the treasurer and I am not aware of any applications being made at this point in time," he said.
